Team,

Auriga (Samantha Lee) is approaching production ramp for their recommendation engine PoC and just signaled a hard start: first production traffic projected week of 2027-12-06. Sales wants a 30-day soft-hold on capacity while procurement finalizes MOA. Can ops confirm fleet availability and a recommended dedicated sizing? Key asks below: 

- Target model: gpt-large-16k (baseline; expect to offer quantized variants)
- Expected steady-state qps: 35 qps (avg), peak 120 qps bursty during batch jobs
- Typical sequence lengths: 512 tokens for inference; some re-ranking flows up to 8k
- Production start window: 2027-12-06 to 2027-12-13 (PoC -> gradual ramp)
- Required SLO: p95 <= 300ms for single-turn recommend flows

Please run an availability check for a 90-day window and propose: minimal dedicated pool (nodes + GPU type), a short-term soft-hold duration we can present to the customer, and any thermal/region constraints (they want us-west primary, with eu fallback for resilience). Attaching the runbook with initial sizing notes.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Final-mile capacity scrub & soft-hold request — Auriga Systems

Mina — thanks for the clear ask. Quick inventory and sizing note (initial pass):

- Recommended baseline: 8 nodes of A100-80GB equivalent (48 total logical GPUs via MIG-like partitioning) to meet steady-state 35 qps with headroom for bursts.
- If they want to keep p95 <= 300ms at peak 120 qps, we should plan for an additional 4 nodes in burst pool (bring-up via autoscale/burst capacity).
- Quantization: int8-friendly profile for gpt-large-16k should drop per-token compute ~2.5x; if they accept int8 we can reduce baseline to 6 nodes.
- KV cache sizing: reserve 96GB per node for long conversations (8k tier) — this affects node memory planning.

Constraints/notes:
- US-WEST (primary) currently has 18 free A100-80GB equivalents outside existing holds. Placing a 30-day soft-hold would consume ~44% of that headroom; recommend we set soft-hold duration to 30 days with automatic release unless MOA countersigned.
- Thermal alerting: a few racks in us-west are on conservative thermal throttle; if we map their pool there we must mark a reduced sustained throughput target (we'd need 1 extra node as buffer).

I've attached a node mapping CSV with node IDs and suggested partitions. If we get a quick thumb-up from sales I can mark the nodes as 'soft-held' in the provisioning system.

[attachment: node-mapping-v2.csv]

— Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Capacity Planning

Karthik — good detail. A few operational points from the inference side: 

- Latency guarantees: with the 8-node baseline and int8 quantization, we can hit p95 ~220–260ms for single-turn 512-token flows. For 8k re-ranking we should expect p95 ~800–1,200ms unless we shard requests; recommend explicit SLAs that exclude heavy batch re-ranking during initial PoC.
- Fallback model: prepare a smaller variant (gpt-medium-8k-quant) that reduces memory by ~40% and can be routed automatically if nodes see thermal throttling. This will preserve availability at slightly lower quality.
- Autoscaler config: set conservative burst policy (scaleUpCooldown 45s, scaleDown 10m) and a safety margin of 20% reserved GPU capacity to prevent noisy neighbor regressions.

Related links: hubspot deal and initial MOA draft would be helpful to pin timelines. I'll sync with Karthik on which nodes to tag.

— Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
